reuse.why: Reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, but adds a new getExpectedScheduleAmount next to the existing getScheduledAmount (which already resolves null/number/range and serves the client) instead of evolving it, so the old midpoint helper stays.

duplication.why: Two shared amount resolvers now coexist with different rules, and forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and schedule-template.ts still compute their own midpoint, so the expected-amount rule lives in at least four places.

placement.why: The resolver lives in shared/schedules.ts and the API field is computed in api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal, the right layers.

scope.why: Changes are on the amount resolution path, the API model and tests; nothing unrelated.

maintainability.why: Callers must guess which of getScheduledAmount / getExpectedScheduleAmount is authoritative, and planning (forecast, templates, UI) silently disagrees with posting and the API.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getExpectedScheduleAmount duplicates getScheduledAmount instead of extending it; forecast-schedules.ts and schedule-template.ts keep inline midpoint arithmetic.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount re-implements getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch under a new name and signature (op instead of inverse).

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount gains an op parameter and an isapprox branch; getScheduledAmount (and its desktop-client callers), forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and schedule-template.ts createScheduleList do not use it.
